To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

for a GLAST‐LET dark matter search, Profile likelihood is the most powerful method to claim a line detection, but also has a higher rate of false detection, whereas the standard χ2 has the lowest rate of false detection but also the worst power to claim detection.
the Profile Likelihood method is best in terms of coverage and worst in terms of power, the standard χ 2 test is the worst in terms of coverage but the best in terms of power.
• Profile likelihood is the best choice for a dark matter discovery claim, but has poor power.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: (i) what are the statistical properties of a GLAST‐LET line search for dark matter; (ii) what is the expected false detection rate and what are the expected power of different statistical tests for a GLAST‐LATT search; and (iii) what is the effect of different systematic errors in the background and in the dark matter spectrum on the false detection rate and the expected power of the different tests.
the statistical methods that can be used to calculate the upper limits and/or the discovery of a line signal from dark matter annihilation in the galactic center, using GLAST‐LAT data.
the development of new methods for analyzing the results of dark matter line searches in gamma‐ray data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, if a dark matter line is detected, the most robust method is Profile Likelihood, but if the dark matter line is not detected, then the standard χ2 method is the most powerful.
the best choice for the method to calculate limits is Profile Likelihood and that for discovery is Bayesian Factors.
for the considered simple case, the Profile Likelihood test is the best method for setting upper limits, while for claiming a discovery the standard χ2 method is the best one.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, if one is interested in the highest possible power, the standard χ ^{2} test is the best choice.
the standard χ2 method has the worst performance in both coverage and power, and that the Bayesian factor method is the best in terms of coverage and power.

the standard χ2 has the worst coverage and power properties, the Bayesian factor is a very good method for calculating upper limits, while the likelihood ratio has the worst power and the best coverage.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, if one is interested in claiming discovery of a signal in a dark matter line, the Profile Likelihood is the method of choice.
the standard method, the χ2 test, has a very poor coverage, but a good power.
the standard method of using the χ2 statistic for upper limits is not appropriate.
